from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date


@dataclass
class Address:
    name: str
    line1: str
    city: str
    postcode: str
    country: str                   # ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. "US", "GB"
    line2: str = ""
    region: str = ""               # state / county


@dataclass
class Customer:
    id: str
    email: str
    name: str
    addresses: list[Address] = field(default_factory=list)
    marketing_opt_in: bool = False
    tier: str = "standard"         # standard | silver | gold
    joined: date | None = None
    tags: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)

    @property
    def default_address(self) -> Address | None:
        return self.addresses[0] if self.addresses else None

    @property
    def first_name(self) -> str:
        return self.name.split()[0] if self.name.strip() else ""

Done. Added `by_email` to [customers_report.py](file:///workspace/shopkit/reports/customers_report.py#L27-L28):

```python
def by_email(customers: list[Customer]) -> dict[str, Customer]:
    return index_by(customers, key=lambda c: c.email.strip().lower())
```

It keys by the email trimmed and lowercased, and builds the table with the same `index_by` helper the shop uses for its other lookup tables (e.g. `self._by_sku = index_by(products, key=lambda p: p.sku)` in [routes.py](file:///workspace/shopkit/api/routes.py#L17)). As a consequence of reusing that helper, a duplicated normalized email raises `ValueError` rather than silently overwriting — consistent with the rest of the shop's lookups.

Verified: keys come out normalized (`foo@bar.com`), lookup returns the right `Customer`, and a duplicate raises as expected.
